analyst_view.overall: Early view: Strasbourg (13th) have lost five of their last six league games and one report says coach Hugo Oliveira is under strong pressure, so a change on the bench during the break cannot be ruled out. Brest (9th) are in good form under Julien Lachuer after 2-0 wins at Lorient and at home to Lyon, though Raphael Le Guen is out for months and Brendan Chardonnet's calf problem was expected to keep him out for up to two weeks from early November.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.3 goals. I lean a little higher: Strasbourg's games have produced 40 goals in 10 (18 for, 22 against), and Brest score 1.8 a game with Ludovic Ajorque leading the line. Brest's patched-up centre-back pairing also gives Giovanni Reyna and Gessime Yassine chances at the other end.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.8 corners. I lean lower: per Statz Strasbourg win the fewest corners in Ligue 1 (2.5 a game) and had one at Toulouse, and Brest play a direct, low-possession game (one corner against Lyon). Neither side builds the sustained pressure that racks up corners.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.5 cards. I lean higher: Brest are 4th for fouls (14.2 a game), and a home side on a bad run with a coach under pressure is prone to frustration. Strasbourg collected three yellows at Toulouse.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.9 shots. I lean higher: Brest average 16.1 shots a game (4th) and Strasbourg 12.6, and Strasbourg's defence gives up plenty. An open game with both sides needing points fits a higher count.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.8 shots on target. I lean higher: Brest are 3rd for shots on target (5.7 a game) and had six against Lyon, and Strasbourg average 4.9. Ten or so looks more likely than eight.
